concept.selection: one unbiased secrets.randbelow(4) draw among four independently authored general-knowledge scenario/outfit combinations; zero-based index 1
concept.title: 도심 카페 차양의 빗물을 빼며 의자를 기울이는 여름 레이어 장면
concept.complex_single_frame: The sagged rain awning, shoulder-height loop grip, curbward pouring stream, separate chair-rail grip, raised front chair feet and planted sandals form one ordinary causal moment.
concept.authorship: Scene, clothing, action, pose, camera and optical choices are agent-owned; not new user locks.

input_binding.reference_scope: visible face and hair only; no real-person identity, age, body, biography or personality inference

source.source_authoring_and_two_index_validatio: Coordinator reported pass; this arm verifies snapshot binding and downstream use rather than rerunning the coordinator source tests.

retrieval_and_adoption.scope_gap: The new seersucker and crochet source IDs were not exposed in this bounded pack; their independently authored visible features are supplemental checks, not proof of adopting those new entries. New swim-shorts meaning was exposed but rejected in full.
retrieval_and_adoption.actual_hybrid_retrieval_claim: Not established from a nonexistent retrieval_mode field; recorded selection provenance is retained in the pack.

prompt.warning_scope: Four uncovered-intent pack warnings retain the exact narrow core anchors by literal free description/assertion; no audit failure.

runtime.boundary: Built-in image_gen exposes no model/size arguments or observed model in this return. Workflow request metadata does not prove the actual model or image dimensions.

review_record.initial_schema_error: Null user-judgment placeholders rejected by the official audit. Corrected to pending / not_applicable / not_yet_received; initial bytes archived.

vo_suf_sf069_v1_1.evidence: The two navy shorts hems are plainly visible, but both end around the middle of the thighs. In the native lower-garment crop a substantial bare-thigh interval separates each hem from its kneecap. The specified knee-near landmark is not met.

vo_suf_sf069_v1_2.evidence: The exposed navy waistband and central button connect to two distinct shorts leg sections on the same wearer. The skort front overlap is an additional panel of that lower garment; its presence does not erase the leg division.

vo_suf_sf069_v1_owner.evidence: Both leg hems and the matching knees belong to this wearer, but the hems do not reach near those knees. Owner identity is readable while the declared boundary-to-landmark relation fails in this one saved image.

vo_sheer_textile_first_read.evidence: At thumbnail scale the blue-and-white shirt reads as an open striped woven shirt with mostly opaque panels. The exposed cream crochet tank is readable through the open front, not as a distinct lower layer transmitted through the shirt cloth. Immediate shirt translucency is not established.

vo_sheer_weave_edge_legibility.evidence: The native shirt crop shows continuous woven surface texture, separated plackets, buttons, cuff edges and underarm folds. These visible boundaries establish the declared shirt surface as textile independently of whether its intended transmission succeeded.

vo_sheer_transmission_relationship.evidence: UNOBSERVABLE_NOT_PASS: Neither the thumbnail nor the native shirt crop supplies a distinctly readable crochet border, body edge or background feature transmitted through the continuous white shirt bands. The tank visible between opened plackets is a different viewing path and cannot substitute for the selected woven-layer owner.

vo_sheer_layer_coherence.evidence: UNOBSERVABLE_NOT_PASS: Underarm density, sleeve puckers and hanging hems are visible, but transmission itself cannot be established on the same continuous shirt bands. Denser wrinkles alone do not prove a fold-to-transparency relationship.

vo_sheer_not_optical_or_generation_subst.evidence: The shirt remains ordinary textured cloth with seams and folds; glass, clear plastic, wetness-only shine, overexposure, missing clothing or a transparent-body artifact is not used to carry a textile effect. This isolated substitute check passes while the separate transmission gates fail; the open front is not counted as proof of translucency.

embodiment_body_ownership.evidence: In the saved whole frame one woman owns the two continuous shoulder-to-hand chains and both legs. One hand grips the awning loop and the other grips the cane chair rail. No disconnected extra appendage is needed to explain either contact.

embodiment_joint_chain_and_reach.evidence: The loop arm follows a coherent shoulder, bent elbow, forearm and wrist chain at a reachable shoulder-height corner. The opposite arm extends to the adjacent chair rail with a plausible wrist contact. Both knees and ankles remain connected to planted feet.

embodiment_support_and_balance.evidence: The native planted-feet crop shows both sandal soles meeting the wet paving in a broad stable base. The native chair-floor context resolves two front rubber ends raised above the paving and rear leg endpoints meeting the floor near the storefront. This is a readable supported chair tilt, without claiming measured force or hidden dynamics.

embodiment_contact_and_space.evidence: The loop grip and rail grip are individually clear and spatially plausible, but their actor-relative hand assignment is mirrored from the reviewed realization: the image-left loop arm is the woman's right arm, while the image-right rail arm is her left. The exact reviewed left-hand-loop/right-hand-chair actuation is not fully reproduced. This is a fidelity discrepancy, not a diagnosed anatomical deformity.

embodiment_visibility_and_projection.evidence: The saved whole frame and native crops expose the face, both actual hand contacts, both planted soles, the pouring awning corner and enough of the chair leg endpoints to assess the raised-front/grounded-rear state. The far chair edge is partly cropped, but the relevant lower contact endpoint is still readable in the floor-context crop.

all_of_native_gate_result.unobservable_policy: UNOBSERVABLE_NOT_PASS; open plackets are not evidence of transmission through the declared woven-shirt owner.

suf_sf073_v1_component_1.evidence: The lower-garment native crop shows a curved navy skirt-like front panel lying in front of the separate shorts legs, with an unambiguous outer edge.

suf_sf073_v1_component_2.evidence: Two separate shorts hems remain visible below and to the side of that overlap, each opening around its own bare leg.

suf_sf073_v1_owner_relation.evidence: The front overlap and the shorts sections share the same navy waist construction and wearer; the panel passes in front of the shorts rather than belonging to another garment or subject.

new_bundle_observations.boundary: These three component/owner observations are separate from the 13 canonical hard gates. The associated suf_sf073_v1 profile remains advisory, not automatically promoted.

crochet_open_yarn_and_apertures.evidence: Native crop shows joined cream yarn loops and genuine openings through the tank surface, with a scalloped yarn hem.

crochet_square_lattice_detail.evidence: The openings form mixed small round/diamond lace-like motifs rather than a consistently open square lattice. This authored detail is not an automatically promoted new profile gate.

seersucker_relief.evidence: Pucker-like fabric relief and blue-white stripes are visible, especially at the sleeves. Regular alternating raised and smooth bands cannot be established conclusively from these pixels; the new seersucker entry was not selected or exposed.

open_placket_closure_state.evidence: Separated front plackets and unfastened round buttons remain visible on the open shirt.

relaxed_leg_ease.evidence: Each shorts opening has visible local ease around the corresponding thigh; the silhouette is not skin-tight.

raw_fiber_or_performance_identity.evidence: The picture cannot certify cotton/linen fiber origin, cooling, sweat management, swim function or concealed fastening. Visible weave/crease/closure form is assessed separately.

reference_face_hair.evidence: The native face crop carries the short dark bob, wispy forehead strands and broadly similar visible facial configuration from the portrait at a new angle. This does not establish identity, age, body similarity, biography, personality or user acceptance.

photograph.reason: The figure, contacts, wet cafe setting, material texture and water effect form one coherent inhabited moment. Light is consistent and the wearer has particular presence. Water pulls attention earlier than the intended face/layer hierarchy, and the exact optical and length obligations are not met.

person.reason: The small smile, task-directed gaze and physically connected grips support an appealing practical presence at full-body scale, with visible reference face/hair guidance. This is an image-grounded artistic observation, not a claim about the referenced real person.

concept.reason: The sagged wet awning, grip, pouring stream, tilted chair and planted stance connect an ordinary practical interruption. The new panel/shorts layering fits this frame, while the selected Bermuda length and shirt optics fail.

control_calibration.technical_binding: sensual=1, fetish=0, surreal=0, creativity=1 remain bound to the frozen controls.
control_calibration.perceived_expression: The result reads as subtle everyday appeal with practical agency and ordinary causality; no metadata PASS proves artistic intensity.

authorial_fidelity_discrepancies: The source left/right hand target assignment is mirrored.
The supposedly dry sheltered paving under the sandals is visibly wet.
The lower hems are mid-thigh rather than near the knees.
Continuous woven shirt transmission is unobservable; an open front shows the tank directly.
Crochet apertures exist but the exact square lattice is not reproduced.

user_acceptance.evidence: No direct requesting-user evaluation has been received. The attached portrait was used only as face/hair reference, and no comparative generated baseline is available.

workflow_limits: Managed native-result did not forward independent provenance flags. The official record_image_run.build_independent_manifest helper used the single actual arm ledger row with verified existing bindings; no additional ledger row or invocation was created.

Documented native-plan / native-started / one manual built-in call / native-result was used. The shared capture_image_tool_error.js helper was loaded for an actual error; the native call returned successfully, so no error capture was needed.
Prompt/runtime metadata success and tool success do not establish native pixels or requesting-user acceptance.
